claude.market_view: The S&P 500 (7,811.54, +0.59% Fri Oct 9) sits near its record after a volatile week. Monday is a thin Columbus Day session with bonds closed, and the 10-year yield is around 5.24%, so expect chop until the bank prints Tuesday and CPI Wednesday; AI and semis sentiment is still fragile after the OpenAI revenue scare.
lessons: Moonshots bought after an after-hours reaction to news everyone had already seen gave back the gap: CLOV (+4-7% AH on 5-star ratings) fell 7.2% and NN fell 5% the next session. Buying an opening gap on overnight news has had negative edge, so these get low confidence and wide stops at most.

Analyst initiations alone were not moonshot catalysts on beaten-down names: KTOS (Barclays $90 target) fell 1.6% and RKLB fell 0.9%. PLTR worked (+3.8%) because two Street calls hit a stock already showing relative strength at a record.

Pre-print run-ups on cost-squeezed names fail: DAL stopped out at -5% when fuel up 62% y/y drove a miss and guide cut. By contrast CCI (+7%), a direct second-order beneficiary of the SpaceX spectrum deal, worked, so fresh structural news beats generic pre-earnings positioning.

picks.thesis: Bloomberg/Reuters reported after Friday's close (Oct 9) that GTCR and Elliott are in advanced talks to take CCC private, with a deal possible as soon as this week. Shares closed $7.02 and traded $7.99 after hours, and a signed deal at a premium would push them toward the take-out price.
picks.catalyst_time: 2026-10-09 after close (report); definitive agreement possible 2026-10-12 onward
picks.main_risk: The ~14% after-hours gap already prices much of a premium, and with no price or signed agreement the open could fade like CLOV/NN did. Talks collapsing invalidates the thesis.

picks.thesis: Mirum announced Sunday (Oct 11) that it will release topline Phase 3 EXPAND results for LIVMARLI in ultra-rare cholestatic liver diseases Monday morning with an 8:30am ET call. A positive label-expansion readout on an already-marketed drug can extend Friday's 5.7% gain intraday.
picks.main_risk: Binary: results aren't public yet. A miss or mixed data on secondary endpoints gaps it down, and even good data may be bought at an already-gapped open.

picks.thesis: First Tracks announced Sunday (Oct 11) Phase 1b cohort 1 topline data for CD122 antagonist ANB033 in celiac disease (gluten challenge) Monday morning with an 8:30am webcast. A clean protective signal in celiac, an indication with no approved drug, could re-rate the ~$1.1B company.
picks.main_risk: Small early cohort and a history of celiac failures. An ambiguous signal or a sell-the-news reaction after the stock held ~$32 would break it.

picks.thesis: Freenome released improved validation data for its next-gen colorectal cancer blood test Sunday at 1pm ET (Oct 11): 80.4% cancer sensitivity at 90% specificity, and advanced precancerous lesion sensitivity up to 18.2% from 13.7%, ahead of an ACG late-breaker Oct 14. First regular session to react is Monday.
picks.main_risk: The improvement is incremental and competitors' tests set a high bar. A 75M-share resale registration from the July IPO is an overhang on any pop.

picks.thesis: Goldman's Oct 8 upgrade to Buy ($230) and Barclays' Oct 9 Overweight initiation ($265) pushed PLTR to a record close of $209.05 (+5.2%) while software rebounded. Breakouts with fresh Street support and relative strength have followed through, and my PLTR moonshot last session made +3.8%.
picks.main_risk: At ~110x forward earnings, any renewed AI-revenue scare (like Thursday's OpenAI report) reverses it, and Monday's thin holiday tape may not carry momentum.

grok.market_view: S&P and Nasdaq futures were slightly higher Sunday night (ES ~7,881, NQ ~31,212) with crude down near $90; Monday is Columbus Day with the bond market closed, so volume may be light, and the week's real tests are bank earnings Tuesday and September CPI Wednesday. Monday has no major US earnings, so stock-specific news (Mirum's Phase 3 readout) and day-2 follow-through on Friday's news should drive the biggest moves.
lessons: Real beat-and-raise drift kept working (PENG added another 6.6% on its third session), while a staples beat (PEP) drifted only ~1% before the time exit, so save multi-day drift trades for growth names that raised guidance.
Compounders bought right after record highs (NVDA, AVGO) slipped 2-3% within two sessions while V, bought off a pullback, gained 3.6%, so add compounders on pullbacks instead of at fresh highs.
Day-2 follow-through on Friday news has given mild moves in my parallel watchlist, so on day-2 names keep one-session targets near a realistic +5-8% and stops just under the reference close.
